title: Inline calls can have logical frames but no separate physical stack frames
summary: A debugger can show inlined calls from compiler debug information even when there is no separate machine-level call for the frame.
applies: Offline stack traceback, symbol matching and debugging information for native programs
detail: The two layers of calls in the source code can share an instruction in the machine code. When reading stack reports, distinguish between inline locations and actual runtime call frames.
boundary: When the compiler does not emit sufficient debugging information, the debugger cannot completely reconstruct all inlining levels.
relevance: The interpreted call chain is one more layer above the actual call instructions in the disassembly.
